title: Introduce credential attestor and release-draft provisioner for credentialed onboards
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: We've had inconsistent metadata attestations for model onboards which causes downstream consumers (serving, billing, and compliance) to fail preflight checks or to require manual remediation. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: 1) a credential attestor service that signs and stores a minimal onboarding credential (JSON Web Token + provenance hash) when a model artifact and its metadata pass a declarative contract; and 2) a release-draft provisioner that synthesizes a changelog stub and annotated release notes draft using attestations and performance-profile deltas so product and docs teams can review before publishing.

What this change does (high level): Adds an attestor microservice (registry/onboard/attestor.py) that implements contract checks, signs a short lived credential with KMS, and stores it in the registry metadata index. Adds a release provisioning hook (registry/hooks/changelog_provisioner.go and registry/cli/preview_release.py) which consumes attestations, computes a concise delta of performance-profile metrics, and emits a templated draft into docs/. The provisioner embeds human-friendly rationale and a short machine-readable summary for automatic release-note aggregation.

Design notes: - Attestation format: JWT with fields {model_id, version, profile_hash, attestor, timestamp, checks_passed} signed by KMS key ring. - Contract checks: schema validation (metadata schema v2), dataset license whitelist, minimum evaluation coverage (coverage > 0.75 on canonical prompt set), and quantization compatibility flag. - Release draft template: includes short summary, risk tier (derived from profile delta), migration notes if any, rolling rollback recommendation, and CI artifact links. - Backwards compatibility: existing onboards without credentials remain readable; the attestor is additive and can be enabled as gate in Linear-driven rollouts.

Migration and rollout plan: 1) Nightly job creates attestations for recent onboards (non-blocking) and stores them in metadata store; 2) After 2 weeks of soak and monitoring of consumer interactions, enable attestation as a soft-gate on staged onboards; 3) Finally flip to hard-gate tied to Dedicated/private deployments requiring signed onboards. Linear tickets ENG-3245 and ENG-3301 track rollout and KMS key rotation.

Testing and validation performed: - Unit tests for schema checks and JWT creation (tests/test_attestor.py). - Integration in staging with preview_release CLI to generate changelog drafts; snapshot tests for template stability. - Canary where provisioner runs on a subset of model uploads and creates draft releases in docs/onboarding/drafts/. - Security review: keys scoped to attestor service account, rotation documented in docs/onboarding/kms_rotation.md.

Checklist:
- [x] Schema validation and unit tests
- [x] End-to-end preview generation in staging
- [x] CI checks for linting and formatting
- [x] Docs draft for credentialed onboarding
- [x] Security review sign-off

Risks and mitigations: - Risk: consumers start depending on credential presence prematurely. Mitigation: attestation is additive and we will use a staged gating approach. - Risk: attestor key compromise. Mitigation: scoped KMS keys, short-lived credentials, rotation plan and audit logs included.

Follow-ups and next PRs: - Add reverse-compatibility converter to backfill attestations for historic models (ENG-3301 follow-up). - Hook provisioner into release annotations aggregator to auto-populate product release notes. - Metrics: add attestation adoption metric and coverage dashboards in Redwood Console (tracked in ENG-3245).
